context_line: Of course — the neutral agreement word (lit. 'known'). Aišku is brisker ('clear!'), be abejo ('without doubt') more emphatic.
source_note: No source read compares žinoma / aišku / be abejo; the shading is my own and should be checked by the owner.

context_line: Of course; clearly — as an answer, a brisk colloquial 'sure, obviously'; as an adverb, 'clearly'. Neutral cousin: žinoma.
Undoubtedly / of course — 'without doubt'; a shade more emphatic and formal than žinoma.
Just a moment — accusative of akimirka 'an instant'; a shop assistant's or receptionist's word. Minutėlę! is the warmer diminutive twin; both fit tu and jūs.
source_note: Deck note on A2-1169 gives 'Minutėlę!'; no external source read.

context_line: Just a minute — said as Minutėlę! (accusative), the diminutive making it friendly; akimirką is the plainer twin.
Great! — neuter adjective used as an exclamation; neutral register. Šaunu is more colloquial, nuostabu/nuostabus stronger ('wonderful'), labai gerai the sober 'very good'.
source_note: No source read grades puiku / šaunu / nuostabu / labai gerai; owner to check.

context_line: Cool! / great! — colloquial, youthful; puiku is the neutral equivalent. Šaunuolis (the person) is 'good lad / well done'.
Wonderful — stronger than puiku; as an exclamation the neuter nuostabu! The card's form is the masculine adjective.
How much is it? — the same question as Kiek kainuoja? with tai ('this/that') said out loud; one picture serves both.
